newsitem.title: USA: Crown sued over Houston refinery emissions.
newsitem.headline: Crown sued over Houston refinery emissions.

text.p: An environmental coalition on Monday filed suit in a Houston federal court seeking to force Crown Central Petroleum Corp to comply with federal and state emissions standards at its Pasadena, Texas refinery.
The suit alleges the 100,000 barrel per day Crown refinery exceeded allowable hydrogen sulfide and sulphur dioxide emissions limits for more than 10,000 hours between May 1992 and December 1996.

The suit, filed by Washington, D.C.-based Trial Lawyers for Public Justice on behalf of the environmental groups, also sought a court order that would force Crown to install monitoring equipment to measure emissions. along with civil damages of up to $25,000 per violation per day.

The Texas Natural Resources Conservation Commission on July 10 cited Crown for alleged emissions violations, but the environmental groups in a statement said the Texas regulators have done little to enforce emissions laws at the refinery.

"TNRCC has done little more than periodically rattle its saber at Crown. Each time, Crown gets off with either a warning or a modest penalty, and it keeps polluting," Neil Carmen of the Sierra Club said.

An industry source said it was likely the TNRCC would take formal enforcement action on the latest series of allegations, which could lead to an order to clean up operations and fines for each violation levied against the refiner.

Randall Trembly, executive vice president for the Baltimore-based company, said Crown met with the environmental groups before the suit was filed to discuss its plans to upgrade equipment and reduce emissions.
"The company plans to vigorously defend the lawsuit," he said in a statement.
Crown's Pasadena refinery has been operated by managers and contractors since February 1996, when union workers were locked out over a contract dispute.

The coalition that filed the suit in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas included the Texans United for a Safe Economy Educational Fund and three of its members, along with the Natural Resources Defense Counsel and the Sierra Club.

Crown in June was sued in a Texas state court by 77 Pasadena residents seeking $50 million in punitive damages stemming from allegations pollution from the refinery was affecting their health and property values. The company also faces a race and sex discrimination suit filed by refinery workers.
